headline: Temporary spending law keeps the federal government funded into early 2024 and extends farm, health, and other expiring programs.
what_it_does: This law prevented a government shutdown by continuing federal funding, mostly at 2023 levels. Agencies covered by four spending bills (including agriculture, veterans affairs, energy, and transportation and housing) were funded through January 19, 2024, and most others through February 2, 2024. It also extended the 2018 farm bill programs, mostly through September 30, 2024, and continued several health, Medicare, Medicaid, and child welfare programs through January 19, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and people who use federal services
who_it_affects.how: Government agencies stayed open and funded into early 2024 instead of shutting down on November 17, 2023.
Farm bill programs such as Price Loss Coverage and Dairy Margin Coverage were extended for the 2024 crop year or through the end of 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Food banks and people who rely on emergency food
who_it_affects.how: The Emergency Food Assistance Program, which sends food to food banks through states, was extended through September 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Patients at community health centers and health workers in underserved areas
who_it_affects.how: Funding for community health centers, the National Health Service Corps, and teaching health centers was extended through January 19, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: People with diabetes and Native American communities
who_it_affects.how: Funding for Type 1 diabetes research and the Special Diabetes Program for Indians was extended through January 19, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Hospitals that serve many low-income patients
who_it_affects.how: Planned cuts to extra Medicaid payments for these hospitals were delayed until January 20, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Doctors and clinical labs paid by Medicare
who_it_affects.how: Certain Medicare payment adjustments for doctors were extended, and lab reporting requirements and related payment cuts were delayed until 2025.

who_it_affects.group: Families in the child welfare system
who_it_affects.how: Grants that help keep families together and support foster care and adoption were funded through January 19, 2024.
The Education Department received flexibility to keep student loan servicing going.
Cost-share help for organic certification and organic data programs were extended through September 2024.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 17, 2023; funding runs through January 19, 2024, or February 2, 2024, depending on the agency, and most farm bill extensions run through September 30, 2024.
